description:
crate-jmap-types/src/error.rs:303-311 declares:

    pub fn too_many_changes() -> Self {
        Self { error_type: \"tooManyChanges\".into(),
               description: None, existing_id: None, limit: None }
    }

immediately followed by error.rs:317-324:

    /// Returns a `tooManyChanges` error with the server's limit included.
    ///
    /// Per RFC 8620 §9.6.1, the `limit` field MUST be present so the client
    /// knows the maximum `maxChanges` value to use on retry.
    pub fn too_many_changes_with_limit(limit: u64) -> Self {
        ...
    }

The doc-comment on `_with_limit` correctly cites RFC 8620 §9.6.1's MUST.
That MUST applies to **the wire form**, not to this particular
constructor. A server author who picks `too_many_changes()` (the
shorter name, found first by IDE completion) produces a wire form
that violates the MUST. The constructor is reachable, public, and
documented as the canonical name (no deprecation, no warning in its
doc-comment).

The same crate already demonstrates the correct pattern for exactly
this situation: error.rs:380-390 marks `unknown_capability()` as
`#[deprecated(note = \"...\")]` and points callers at
`unknown_capability_with_detail`. The pattern was already established;
it was just not applied to `too_many_changes`.

What a caller depending on this API in production accepts:

1. The constructor is a footgun. A server author searching for
   \"tooManyChanges\" sees `too_many_changes()` (no args) and uses it.
   The wire output is noncompliant. The client can't recover with a
   smaller `maxChanges` because the limit is missing.
2. No compile-time signal, no rustdoc warning, no `#[deprecated]`.
3. The corresponding test (error.rs:646-651) asserts the bare
   constructor's wire form does NOT contain `\"description\"`, which
   reinforces that the field-absent shape is intentional. The test
   does not flag that the shape is RFC-noncompliant.

Fix candidates:
- Mark `too_many_changes()` as `#[deprecated(since = \"0.1.2\", note =
  \"always use too_many_changes_with_limit to include the limit per
  RFC 8620 §9.6.1\")]`, mirroring the existing `unknown_capability`
  pattern. Add `#[allow(deprecated)]` on the test.
- Or: remove `too_many_changes()` entirely. Breaking change at the
  source level but the wire form was already broken.
- Or: change the bare constructor to require a limit
  (`too_many_changes(limit: u64)`) and remove the `_with_limit`
  variant. Breaking change.

Cross-reference: JMAP-6xs8.10 already filed a related correctness bug
in `SetError.extra` doc-comments; this finding is a separate
contract-shape defect.
title: JmapError::too_many_changes() produces wire-noncompliant error (RFC 8620 9.6.1 says limit MUST be present)
